profile.name: Brooke Winkler
profile.degreeLine: B.S. Mechanical Engineering & Aerospace Engineering · Honors Program · Michigan Technological University · Expected April 2030
profile.target: Seeking a Summer 2027 motorsports engineering internship
profile.objective: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering student at Michigan Technological University (Honors Program, Class of 2030) with four years of FIRST Robotics design, fabrication, electrical, and leadership experience, including a FIRST Impact Award and World Championship qualification. Independent research into the 2026 Formula 1 power unit regulations and their effect on racing.

experience.role: Captain — Design, Strategy, Build & Electrical Lead
bullets: Ran match strategy, scouting and real-time pit decisions through six-week build-and-compete seasons on a rookie-heavy roster.
Tuned robot parameters and operational values between and during matches — hands-on telemetry work that made the calls I made executable.
Owned the technical chain end to end: SolidWorks design, CNC / 3D-print / laser fabrication, wiring, and Java + WPILib bring-up.
Mentored newer members into independent ownership of design, build, pit and match operations.
experience.result: FIRST Impact Award · World Championship qualifier · regional & state competition runs

bullets: Worked inside a top-tier motorsports event weekend, supporting media and race-adjacent operations and seeing how a professional paddock is run.
Filed coverage with local news outlets — turning raw event detail into a story a wider audience could follow.
Built the outbound engine from nothing — process, materials, qualification criteria and client pipeline.
Helped generate the revenue that funded an entire FRC competition robot.

analysis.role: 2026 Formula 1 Power Unit Regulations — Independent Research
bullets: Reading the 2026 PU regulations clause by clause: the near-50/50 ICE-to-electric split, deployment modes, sustainable fuels, active aero.
Mapping each rule to its on-track consequence — deployment strategy, race rhythm, overtaking mechanics, and how the field reshapes.
Writing it as a briefing I would defend line by line — the discipline I want to apply to real team data.
Senior-year captain after three varsity seasons — reading conditions, committing to a plan, holding rhythm under a clock.
Ran backstage technical operations and crews across productions, solving logistics and timing problems live.
Mentored two FTC teams, including standing up a rookie organisation and coaching one to the Michigan State Championship.

honors: 3× Top Technician in the State of Michigan
FIRST Impact Award · World Championship Qualifier

goal.label: Next
goal.text: Formula 1, IndyCar, IMSA or an OEM team — anywhere strategy and telemetry are taken seriously. Building toward Formula SAE at Michigan Tech and eager to put hands on a real data stack.
